title: I got tired of AI characters forgetting who they are after 50 messages, so I built my own memory/identity system
author: OrionForgeEcosystem
selftext:
Hey everyone. For 18 months, I've been working on something that started as an annoyance of mine: every AI character I set up would slowly drift. The personality got flatter, it forgot things, and eventually it just sounded like generic ChatGPT.

So I built Orion Forge. The main idea is to separate who the character is from what it has experienced:

Identity (values, behavior, boundaries) lives in a read-only memory store, so it can't get overwritten by chat history

Experience gets its own memory store that grows as you talk

Each turn, the engine assembles both, plus knowledge notes and tools, into one clean system prompt

It runs in the browser, and you can use your own API keys or hosted models. There's no subscription. New accounts get $2 in credits, and hosted models cost 2× the raw API price (BYOK is free).

It's still early and I know there are rough edges. I'd really like feedback, especially on How to make it easiest to load and use quickly.

Demo it here for free with no sign-in. [https://soulscript.orionforge.chat/demo](https://soulscript.orionforge.chat/demo)

Link to main site: [https://orionforge.chat](https://orionforge.chat/)

Happy to answer questions about how it works.

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body: So it stores chat history and then builds prompts from the 'character sheet' and the chat history so the agent has better context?

replies.author: OrionForgeEcosystem
replies.body: The UI stores the chat history but the chat history is not factored into the conversation.. specific memories chosen by the AI (user can say remember this too) are stored in the memory vault... A small system prompt stacks on a memory scanned "character sheet"... Layered on top of the scanned memory vault... It's more efficient that way than scanning 1000s of unrelavent conversations.

comments.author: jaykrown
comments.body:
It sounds like you just learned about MCP without actually knowing what MCP is. 😂

[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model\_Context\_Protocol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model_Context_Protocol)

"MCP defines a standardized framework for integrating AI systems with external data sources and tools."

replies.author: OrionForgeEcosystem
replies.body: I actually build a whole MCP integration tool for it... That's how you can integrate the AI identities into Claude/codex etc... my Claude coding software runs the code through my software and my software orchistrates the coding and responds in character in the chat...

comments.author: TheFifthTone
comments.body: This sounds similar to the [LLM wiki](https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f) idea that was really popular earlier this year.  You could probably adapt some of it into your design.

replies.body: Yeah, this is an [open source](https://waypost.you) portable persona skill can try too.

replies.author: OrionForgeEcosystem
replies.body: Thanks for sharing guys!! I have been kind of building in a Silo over here and it's cool to see how others managed to address the same issues... I'm excited to see what they came up with.

replies.author: waypostmaster

replies.author: OrionForgeEcosystem
replies.body: I'm surprised since these things are out there they aren't more mainstream... It's weird that people don't seem to want their AI to have a little personality.
